import os
from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock
import repo_manager


def test_clone_repo_with_fork_clones_from_upstream(tmp_path):
    """Should clone from upstream_url, not the fork clone_url."""
    calls = []

    def fake_run(cmd, **kwargs):
        calls.append(list(cmd))
        result = MagicMock()
        if len(cmd) >= 2 and cmd[1] == 'clone':
            repo_path = cmd[-1]
            os.makedirs(repo_path, exist_ok=True)
            result.returncode = 0
            result.stdout = ""
            result.stderr = ""
        elif len(cmd) >= 2 and cmd[1] == 'rev-parse':
            result.returncode = 0
            result.stdout = "abc123def456\n"
            result.stderr = ""
        elif len(cmd) >= 2 and cmd[1] == 'remote':
            result.returncode = 0
            result.stdout = ""
            result.stderr = ""
        return result

    repo_dir = str(tmp_path / "repos")
    with patch('subprocess.run', side_effect=fake_run):
        repo_manager.clone_repo_with_fork(
            clone_url="http/workspace/gitcode.com/myuser/myrepo.git",
            repo_dir=repo_dir,
            repo_name="myrepo",
            upstream_url="http/workspace/gitcode.com/upstream/myrepo.git"
        )

    clone_cmds = [c for c in calls if len(c) >= 2 and c[1] == 'clone']
    assert len(clone_cmds) > 0, "Should have at least one clone command"
    cmd_str = " ".join(clone_cmds[0])
    assert "upstream/myrepo.git" in cmd_str, \
        f"Clone should use upstream URL, got: {cmd_str}"


def test_clone_repo_with_fork_adds_fork_remote(tmp_path):
    """Should add fork_origin remote pointing to the fork URL."""
    calls = []

    def fake_run(cmd, **kwargs):
        calls.append(list(cmd))
        result = MagicMock()
        if len(cmd) >= 2 and cmd[1] == 'clone':
            repo_path = cmd[-1]
            os.makedirs(repo_path, exist_ok=True)
            result.returncode = 0
            result.stdout = ""
            result.stderr = ""
        elif len(cmd) >= 2 and cmd[1] == 'rev-parse':
            result.returncode = 0
            result.stdout = "abc123def456\n"
            result.stderr = ""
        elif len(cmd) >= 2 and cmd[1] == 'remote':
            result.returncode = 0
            result.stdout = ""
            result.stderr = ""
        return result

    repo_dir = str(tmp_path / "repos")
    fork_url = "http/workspace/gitcode.com/myuser/myrepo.git"
    with patch('subprocess.run', side_effect=fake_run):
        repo_manager.clone_repo_with_fork(
            clone_url=fork_url,
            repo_dir=repo_dir,
            repo_name="myrepo",
            upstream_url="http/workspace/gitcode.com/upstream/myrepo.git"
        )

    remote_cmds = [c for c in calls if len(c) >= 2 and c[1] == 'remote']
    assert len(remote_cmds) > 0, "Should have at least one remote command"
    assert 'fork_origin' in remote_cmds[0], \
        f"Remote should be named 'fork_origin', got: {remote_cmds[0]}"
    remote_url = remote_cmds[0][-1]
    assert 'myuser/myrepo' in remote_url, \
        f"Remote URL should point to fork, got: {remote_url}"


def test_clone_repo_with_fork_returns_path_on_success(tmp_path):
    """Should return the repo path on successful clone from upstream."""
    def fake_run(cmd, **kwargs):
        result = MagicMock()
        if len(cmd) >= 2 and cmd[1] == 'clone':
            repo_path = cmd[-1]
            os.makedirs(repo_path, exist_ok=True)
            result.returncode = 0
            result.stdout = ""
            result.stderr = ""
        elif len(cmd) >= 2 and cmd[1] == 'rev-parse':
            result.returncode = 0
            result.stdout = "abc123def456\n"
            result.stderr = ""
        elif len(cmd) >= 2 and cmd[1] == 'remote':
            result.returncode = 0
            result.stdout = ""
            result.stderr = ""
        return result

    repo_dir = str(tmp_path / "repos")
    with patch('subprocess.run', side_effect=fake_run):
        result = repo_manager.clone_repo_with_fork(
            clone_url="http/workspace/gitcode.com/myuser/myrepo.git",
            repo_dir=repo_dir,
            repo_name="myrepo",
            upstream_url="http/workspace/gitcode.com/upstream/myrepo.git"
        )

    expected_path = os.path.join(repo_dir, "myrepo")
    assert result == expected_path, \
        f"Should return repo path {expected_path}, got {result}"


def test_clone_repo_with_fork_empty_repo_returns_none(tmp_path):
    """Should return None when clone produces an empty repo (HEAD check fails)."""
    def fake_run(cmd, **kwargs):
        result = MagicMock()
        if len(cmd) >= 2 and cmd[1] == 'clone':
            repo_path = cmd[-1]
            os.makedirs(repo_path, exist_ok=True)
            result.returncode = 0
            result.stdout = ""
            result.stderr = ""
        elif len(cmd) >= 2 and cmd[1] == 'rev-parse':
            result.returncode = 128
            result.stdout = ""
            result.stderr = "fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD'"
        elif len(cmd) >= 2 and cmd[1] == 'remote':
            result.returncode = 0
            result.stdout = ""
            result.stderr = ""
        return result

    repo_dir = str(tmp_path / "repos")
    with patch('subprocess.run', side_effect=fake_run):
        with patch('time.sleep'):
            result = repo_manager.clone_repo_with_fork(
                clone_url="http/workspace/gitcode.com/myuser/myrepo.git",
                repo_dir=repo_dir,
                repo_name="myrepo",
                upstream_url="http/workspace/gitcode.com/upstream/myrepo.git"
            )

    assert result is None, \
        f"Should return None for empty repo, got {result}"


def test_clone_repo_from_source_still_works(tmp_path):
    """Existing clone_repo_from_source function should still work correctly."""
    def fake_run(cmd, **kwargs):
        result = MagicMock()
        if len(cmd) >= 2 and cmd[1] == 'clone':
            repo_path = cmd[-1]
            os.makedirs(repo_path, exist_ok=True)
            result.returncode = 0
            result.stdout = ""
            result.stderr = ""
        return result

    repo_dir = str(tmp_path / "repos")
    with patch('subprocess.run', side_effect=fake_run):
        result = repo_manager.clone_repo_from_source(
            owner="someowner",
            repo="somerepo",
            repo_dir=repo_dir,
            issue_url="http/workspace/gitcode.com/someowner/somerepo/issues/1"
        )

    expected_path = os.path.join(repo_dir, "somerepo")
    assert result == expected_path, \
        f"Should return repo path {expected_path}, got {result}"
